title: ee.daemon.response.v1
description: Length-prefixed JSON response envelope returned by the optional `ee daemon` Unix-domain socket RPC introduced by bd-oja31 (SRR1 hot-mode skeleton). The wire framing matches `ee.daemon.request.v1`: 4-byte big-endian unsigned length followed by exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON. `request_id`, `agent_id`, and optional `workspace_id` echo the request. Exactly one of `result` or `error` is populated. `ee.daemon.capabilities` advertises envelope schemas, methods, authorization, and nested `method_schemas`; clients must fall back locally when `ee.daemon.search` or its exact request/response schema ids are absent. A successful search result is the strict `ee.daemon.search.response.v1` wrapper around canonical `ee.response.v2` machine output, human output, and an honest reuse contract: daemon process and default embedder are process-scoped while the search index is constructed per request.

request_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's request_id. A response whose request_id does not match the most recent request on the same connection MUST be treated as a framing error and the connection torn down.

agent_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's agent_id. Pre-parse refusal responses use a sentinel such as `<unknown>` because the daemon could not safely read the caller's envelope.

workspace_id.description: Echo of the request envelope's optional workspace_id when present. Absent when the request omitted it or when the daemon refused before parsing the request envelope.

result.description: Method-specific success payload. Capability results include `protocol`, envelope schemas, methods, authorization, `method_schemas`, and forward-compatibility policy. Search results use strict `ee.daemon.search.response.v1`; other results retain their registered method-specific contracts.

error.description: Populated when the method failed. Registered codes include `daemon_unknown_method`, `daemon_method_unauthorized`, `daemon_request_decode_failed`, `daemon_request_schema_mismatch`, `daemon_context_params_invalid`, `daemon_context_deadline_exceeded`, `daemon_context_execution_failed`, `daemon_search_params_invalid`, and `daemon_search_execution_failed`, plus method-specific write, telemetry, lifecycle, and authorization codes. Consumers must tolerate unknown codes and opt-in CLI clients must use canonical local search when daemon search fails.

degraded_codes.description: Bare degraded-code strings the daemon attached to the response. The CLI client maps each entry onto a full `ee.response.v2` `degraded[]` entry (severity/repair pulled from the canonical taxonomy in docs/degraded_code_taxonomy.md). Empty array when nothing degraded.
